import Mathlib

structure BinaryMaxHeap where
  storage : List Int
deriving Inhabited

namespace BinaryMaxHeap

def len (h : BinaryMaxHeap) : Nat :=
  h.storage.length

def get (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (i : Nat) : Int :=
  h.storage.getD i 0 -- Safe access with default

def parent (i : Nat) : Nat := (i - 1) / 2

def is_heap (h : BinaryMaxHeap) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, 0 < i ∧ i < h.len → h.get i ≤ h.get (parent i)

def view (h : BinaryMaxHeap) : Multiset Int :=
  Multiset.ofList h.storage

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def push_precond (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  is_heap h ∧ h.len < 1023 -- Limited capacity as per spec example
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- The list-level heap invariant: every non-root position is dominated by its parent. -/
def IsHeapList (l : List Int) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, 0 < j → j < l.length → l.getD j 0 ≤ l.getD (parent j) 0

/-- Heap invariant everywhere except possibly at the "hole" index `i`. -/
def HeapExcept (l : List Int) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, 0 < j → j < l.length → j ≠ i → l.getD j 0 ≤ l.getD (parent j) 0

/-- The value `v` travelling through the hole dominates the children of the hole. -/
def HoleDom (l : List Int) (i : Nat) (v : Int) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, 0 < j → j < l.length → parent j = i → l.getD j 0 ≤ v

/-- The children of the hole are also dominated by the hole's parent. -/
def HoleDomParent (l : List Int) (i : Nat) : Prop :=
  0 < i → ∀ j, 0 < j → j < l.length → parent j = i → l.getD j 0 ≤ l.getD (parent i) 0

theorem parent_lt (i : Nat) (hi : 0 < i) : parent i < i := by
  have h := Nat.div_le_self (i - 1) 2
  simp only [parent]
  omega

/-- Bubble the value `v` up from the hole at index `i`: while the parent is smaller
than `v`, move the parent down into the hole and continue from the parent. -/
def siftUp (l : List Int) (i : Nat) (v : Int) : List Int :=
  match i with
  | 0 => l.set 0 v
  | (k + 1) =>
      if l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0 < v then
        siftUp (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0)) (parent (k + 1)) v
      else
        l.set (k + 1) v
termination_by i
decreasing_by exact parent_lt (k + 1) (Nat.succ_pos k)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def push (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : push_precond h v) : BinaryMaxHeap :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  ⟨siftUp (h.storage ++ [v]) h.len v⟩
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def push_postcond (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int) (result : BinaryMaxHeap)
    (_ : push_precond h v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  is_heap result ∧
  result.len = h.len + 1 ∧
  result.view = h.view + {v}
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
section SiftUpLemmas

/-! ### Basic `getD`/`set` bookkeeping -/

theorem getD_set_self (l : List Int) (i : Nat) (x : Int) (hi : i < l.length) :
    (l.set i x).getD i 0 = x := by
  induction l generalizing i with
  | nil => simp at hi
  | cons a t ih =>
    cases i with
    | zero => simp
    | succ k =>
      simp only [List.set_cons_succ, List.getD_cons_succ]
      exact ih k (by simp only [List.length_cons] at hi; omega)

theorem getD_set_ne (l : List Int) (i j : Nat) (x : Int) (hne : j ≠ i) :
    (l.set i x).getD j 0 = l.getD j 0 := by
  induction l generalizing i j with
  | nil => simp
  | cons a t ih =>
    cases i with
    | zero =>
      cases j with
      | zero => exact absurd rfl hne
      | succ k => simp
    | succ m =>
      cases j with
      | zero => simp
      | succ k =>
        simp only [List.set_cons_succ, List.getD_cons_succ]
        exact ih m k (by omega)

theorem getD_append_left (l₁ l₂ : List Int) (j : Nat) (hj : j < l₁.length) :
    (l₁ ++ l₂).getD j 0 = l₁.getD j 0 := by
  induction l₁ generalizing j with
  | nil => simp at hj
  | cons a t ih =>
    cases j with
    | zero => simp
    | succ k =>
      simp only [List.cons_append, List.getD_cons_succ]
      exact ih k (by simp only [List.length_cons] at hj; omega)

theorem getD_append_self (l₁ : List Int) (x : Int) :
    (l₁ ++ [x]).getD l₁.length 0 = x := by
  induction l₁ with
  | nil => simp
  | cons a t ih => simp

/-- Overwriting position `i` exchanges the old entry for the new one in the multiset view. -/
theorem ofList_set (l : List Int) (i : Nat) (x : Int) (hi : i < l.length) :
    (Multiset.ofList (l.set i x)) + {l.getD i 0} = (Multiset.ofList l) + {x} := by
  induction l generalizing i with
  | nil => simp at hi
  | cons a t ih =>
    cases i with
    | zero =>
      simp only [List.set_cons_zero, List.getD_cons_zero]
      show ({x} + Multiset.ofList t) + {a} = ({a} + Multiset.ofList t) + {x}
      abel
    | succ k =>
      have hk : k < t.length := by simp only [List.length_cons] at hi; omega
      simp only [List.set_cons_succ, List.getD_cons_succ]
      calc {a} + Multiset.ofList (t.set k x) + {t.getD k 0}
          = {a} + (Multiset.ofList (t.set k x) + {t.getD k 0}) := by abel
        _ = {a} + (Multiset.ofList t + {x}) := by rw [ih k hk]
        _ = {a} + Multiset.ofList t + {x} := by abel

/-- Dropping `v` into the hole at `i` restores the full heap invariant, provided the
children of the hole are dominated by `v` and `v` is dominated by the hole's parent. -/
theorem setHole_heap (l : List Int) (i : Nat) (v : Int) (hi : i < l.length)
    (hexc : HeapExcept l i) (hdom : HoleDom l i v)
    (htop : 0 < i → v ≤ l.getD (parent i) 0) : IsHeapList (l.set i v) := by
  intro j hj0 hjlen
  rw [List.length_set] at hjlen
  by_cases hji : j = i
  · subst hji
    have hpj : parent j < j := parent_lt j hj0
    rw [getD_set_self l j v hi, getD_set_ne l j (parent j) v (by omega)]
    exact htop hj0
  · rw [getD_set_ne l i j v hji]
    by_cases hpj : parent j = i
    · rw [hpj, getD_set_self l i v hi]
      exact hdom j hj0 hjlen hpj
    · rw [getD_set_ne l i (parent j) v hpj]
      exact hexc j hj0 hjlen hji

/-- Full correctness of the bubble-up loop: it keeps the length, exchanges the hole's
old entry for `v` in the multiset view, and restores the heap invariant. -/
theorem siftUp_spec : ∀ (n i : Nat), i ≤ n → ∀ (l : List Int) (v : Int), i < l.length →
    HeapExcept l i → HoleDom l i v → HoleDomParent l i →
    (siftUp l i v).length = l.length ∧
      (Multiset.ofList (siftUp l i v)) + {l.getD i 0} = (Multiset.ofList l) + {v} ∧
      IsHeapList (siftUp l i v) := by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro i hi l v hil hexc hdom _
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := Nat.le_zero.mp hi
    have h0 : siftUp l 0 v = l.set 0 v := by rw [siftUp]
    rw [h0]
    exact ⟨List.length_set, ofList_set l 0 v hil,
      setHole_heap l 0 v hil hexc hdom (fun hcon => absurd hcon (lt_irrefl 0))⟩
  | succ n ih =>
    intro i hi l v hil hexc hdom hpar
    match i with
    | 0 =>
      have h0 : siftUp l 0 v = l.set 0 v := by rw [siftUp]
      rw [h0]
      exact ⟨List.length_set, ofList_set l 0 v hil,
        setHole_heap l 0 v hil hexc hdom (fun hcon => absurd hcon (lt_irrefl 0))⟩
    | (k + 1) =>
      have hplt : parent (k + 1) < k + 1 := parent_lt (k + 1) (Nat.succ_pos k)
      have hpl : parent (k + 1) < l.length := by omega
      have heq : siftUp l (k + 1) v =
          if l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0 < v then
            siftUp (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0)) (parent (k + 1)) v
          else l.set (k + 1) v := by rw [siftUp]
      rw [heq]
      by_cases hc : l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0 < v
      · rw [if_pos hc]
        -- the parent's value moves down into the hole, and the hole moves up
        have e1 : HeapExcept (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0)) (parent (k + 1)) := by
          intro j hj0 hjlen hjne
          rw [List.length_set] at hjlen
          by_cases hjk : j = k + 1
          · subst hjk
            rw [getD_set_self l (k + 1) _ hil,
              getD_set_ne l (k + 1) (parent (k + 1)) _ (by omega)]
          · rw [getD_set_ne l (k + 1) j _ hjk]
            by_cases hpk : parent j = k + 1
            · rw [hpk, getD_set_self l (k + 1) _ hil]
              exact hpar (Nat.succ_pos k) j hj0 hjlen hpk
            · rw [getD_set_ne l (k + 1) (parent j) _ hpk]
              exact hexc j hj0 hjlen hjk
        have e2 : HoleDom (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0)) (parent (k + 1)) v := by
          intro j hj0 hjlen hpj
          rw [List.length_set] at hjlen
          by_cases hjk : j = k + 1
          · subst hjk
            rw [getD_set_self l (k + 1) _ hil]
            exact le_of_lt hc
          · rw [getD_set_ne l (k + 1) j _ hjk]
            have hle := hexc j hj0 hjlen hjk
            rw [hpj] at hle
            exact le_of_lt (lt_of_le_of_lt hle hc)
        have e3 : HoleDomParent (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0)) (parent (k + 1)) := by
          intro hp0 j hj0 hjlen hpj
          rw [List.length_set] at hjlen
          have hppne : parent (parent (k + 1)) ≠ k + 1 := by
            have := parent_lt (parent (k + 1)) hp0; omega
          have hstep : l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0 ≤ l.getD (parent (parent (k + 1))) 0 :=
            hexc (parent (k + 1)) hp0 hpl (by omega)
          rw [getD_set_ne l (k + 1) (parent (parent (k + 1))) _ hppne]
          by_cases hjk : j = k + 1
          · subst hjk
            rw [getD_set_self l (k + 1) _ hil]
            exact hstep
          · rw [getD_set_ne l (k + 1) j _ hjk]
            have hle := hexc j hj0 hjlen hjk
            rw [hpj] at hle
            exact le_trans hle hstep
        obtain ⟨hlen', hms', hheap'⟩ :=
          ih (parent (k + 1)) (by omega) (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0)) v
            (by rw [List.length_set]; exact hpl) e1 e2 e3
        refine ⟨by rw [hlen', List.length_set], ?_, hheap'⟩
        rw [getD_set_ne l (k + 1) (parent (k + 1)) _ (by omega)] at hms'
        refine add_right_cancel (b := ({l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0} : Multiset Int)) ?_
        calc Multiset.ofList (siftUp (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0))
                (parent (k + 1)) v) + {l.getD (k + 1) 0}
                + {l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0}
            = (Multiset.ofList (siftUp (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0))
                (parent (k + 1)) v) + {l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0}) + {l.getD (k + 1) 0} := by
              abel
          _ = (Multiset.ofList (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0)) + {v})
                + {l.getD (k + 1) 0} := by rw [hms']
          _ = (Multiset.ofList (l.set (k + 1) (l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0))
                + {l.getD (k + 1) 0}) + {v} := by abel
          _ = (Multiset.ofList l + {l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0}) + {v} := by
              rw [ofList_set l (k + 1) _ hil]
          _ = Multiset.ofList l + {v} + {l.getD (parent (k + 1)) 0} := by abel
      · rw [if_neg hc]
        exact ⟨List.length_set, ofList_set l (k + 1) v hil,
          setHole_heap l (k + 1) v hil hexc hdom (fun _ => not_lt.mp hc)⟩

end SiftUpLemmas
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem push_postcond_satisfied (h : BinaryMaxHeap) (v : Int)
    (h_precond : push_precond h v) :
    push_postcond h v (push h v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  obtain ⟨hheap, _⟩ := h_precond
  simp only [is_heap, len, get] at hheap
  -- the new element is appended, so the hole sits at index `h.storage.length`
  have hil : h.storage.length < (h.storage ++ [v]).length := by simp
  have hexc : HeapExcept (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length := by
    intro j hj0 hjlen hjne
    simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] at hjlen
    have hjs : j < h.storage.length := by omega
    have hpj : parent j < j := parent_lt j hj0
    rw [getD_append_left _ _ _ hjs, getD_append_left _ _ _ (by omega)]
    exact hheap j ⟨hj0, hjs⟩
  -- no index can have the freshly appended last slot as its parent
  have hdom : HoleDom (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length v := by
    intro j hj0 hjlen hpj
    simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] at hjlen
    have := parent_lt j hj0
    omega
  have hpar : HoleDomParent (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length := by
    intro _ j hj0 hjlen hpj
    simp only [List.length_append, List.length_singleton] at hjlen
    have := parent_lt j hj0
    omega
  obtain ⟨hlen, hms, hheap'⟩ :=
    siftUp_spec h.storage.length h.storage.length le_rfl (h.storage ++ [v]) v hil hexc hdom hpar
  rw [getD_append_self] at hms
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro j hj
    exact hheap' j hj.1 hj.2
  · show (siftUp (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length v).length = h.storage.length + 1
    rw [hlen]
    simp
  · show Multiset.ofList (siftUp (h.storage ++ [v]) h.storage.length v)
      = Multiset.ofList h.storage + {v}
    have hcast : Multiset.ofList (h.storage ++ [v]) = Multiset.ofList h.storage + {v} := by
      rfl
    rw [hcast] at hms
    exact add_right_cancel hms
  -- !benchmark @end proof

end BinaryMaxHeap

**LEAN VERIFIED.** The only remaining diagnostics are two `unused variable` warnings on teacher-owned scaffold lines (the `v` in `push_precond`, the `h_precond` in `push`'s signature).

## What was wrong
The previous session had a complete implementation (`siftUp` + `push`) and the auxiliary predicates, but the `proof` region was still `sorry` — which is why the independent verifier rejected it before Lean ever ran. Nothing else had been compile-checked either.

## What I did
Edited only `auxcode`, `lemma`, and `proof`:

- **auxcode**: added `termination_by i` to `siftUp` so the well-founded recursion doesn't rely on Lean's measure guess. Implementation itself unchanged (append `v`, bubble up by sliding a too-small parent down into the hole).
- **lemma** (`Solution.lean:83`–`254`): the real work.
  - `getD_set_self`, `getD_set_ne`, `getD_append_left`, `getD_append_self` — index bookkeeping, all proved by induction.
  - `ofList_set`: `↑(l.set i x) + {l[i]} = ↑l + {x}` — the additive (cancellation-friendly) form of "overwriting swaps one element in the multiset view".
  - `setHole_heap`: dropping `v` into the hole restores `IsHeapList` given `HeapExcept`, `HoleDom`, and `v ≤ l[parent i]`.
  - `siftUp_spec`: the main induction (over a fuel bound on `i`, so it uses plain `Nat.rec`), simultaneously proving length preservation, `↑(siftUp l i v) + {l[i]} = ↑l + {v}`, and `IsHeapList (siftUp l i v)`. The recursive branch re-establishes all three hole hypotheses at `parent i`, including the sibling case (sibling `≤ l[parent]` `< v`).
- **proof**: instantiates the spec at hole index `h.storage.length`. `HoleDom`/`HoleDomParent` are discharged by vacuity there (nothing can have the fresh last slot as parent, since `parent j < j`), `HeapExcept` comes from `is_heap h` via `getD_append_left`, and the multiset postcondition falls out by `add_right_cancel` after `getD_append_self` gives `l[h.len] = v`.

## Semantic audit
- Precond/postcond regions untouched; the capacity bound `h.len < 1023` is still required and not exploited (the implementation is correct without it, so the problem is not weakened).
- All three postconditions proven: heap invariant, `len + 1`, `view = h.view + {v}`.
- Helpers are genuine predicates/proofs — no `:= 0`, `:= True`, `decide`, or axioms; the `sorry` is gone.
- Edge cases: empty heap (`i = 0` base case yields `[v]`); root reached mid-bubble (base case, no parent comparison); duplicate values (multiset formulation, `add_right_cancel` valid); **all-negative inputs** — `get`'s `0` default is only ever reached at out-of-range indices, and every comparison in `is_heap`/`IsHeapList`/`siftUp` is at some `j < length` with `parent j < j < length`, so the default value never participates and a heap of negatives is handled like any other.

analysis:
The student’s submission does implement the intended push operation for a binary max-heap using the expected algorithmic idea:

- It represents the heap as an array/list (`storage : List Int`).
- `push` first appends the new value `v` at the end: `h.storage ++ [v]`.
- It then calls `siftUp ... h.len v`, which bubbles `v` upward by repeatedly comparing it with its parent and moving the parent down when the parent is smaller.
- This is exactly the standard binary max-heap insertion algorithm described in the problem.

More specifically, `siftUp` is not a dummy wrapper or a call to an external heap library. It is a recursive implementation from scratch:
- Base case: if index is `0`, write `v` into the root.
- Recursive case: if parent value `< v`, move the parent down into the current hole and recurse on the parent index.
- Otherwise, place `v` at the current index.

This matches “insert at the end and bubble it up to restore the heap property.”

On the verification side:
- The student provides supporting predicates and lemmas (`IsHeapList`, `HeapExcept`, `HoleDom`, etc.).
- There is a full proof structure culminating in `push_postcond_satisfied`.
- There is no use of `sorry`, `admit`, axioms, empty bodies, or placeholder implementations.
- There is no use of a built-in heap push/sort routine to bypass the task.

Potential oddities like using `getD ... 0` for safe indexing do not violate the algorithmic requirement, because the actual push implementation works by appending then sifting within valid indices, and the proof infrastructure is substantial rather than evasive.
